answer: The effective federal funds rate averaged 19.04% in July 1981 (monthly average, not seasonally adjusted). Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, FRED series FEDFUNDS.

The median sales price of houses sold in the U.S. was $442,600 in the fourth quarter of 2022 (quarterly, not seasonally adjusted). This series covers new houses only; FRED now titles it 'Median Sales Price of New Houses Sold for the United States'. Source: U.S. Census Bureau and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, FRED series MSPUS.

The U.S. unemployment rate averaged about 3.7% over the 12 months of 2019 (3.675% unrounded, the simple mean of the monthly seasonally adjusted rates, which ranged from 4.0% in January to 3.5% in September). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, FRED series UNRATE.

5 months. Year-over-year headline CPI inflation (CPI-U, seasonally adjusted) was above 4% in January through May 2023: 6.3%, 6.0%, 4.9%, 5.0% and 4.1%. From June (3.1%) to December (3.3%) it stayed below 4%. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, FRED series CPIAUCSL (percent change from a year ago).
The highest weekly average 30-year fixed mortgage rate in 2023 was 7.79%, for the week ending Thursday, October 26, 2023. Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, FRED series MORTGAGE30US.

The U.S. added about 1,459,000 nonfarm payroll jobs (roughly 1.46 million) from December 2023 to December 2024. Seasonally adjusted total nonfarm employment rose from 156,857 thousand to 158,316 thousand. These are the currently published figures, which include benchmark revisions and are lower than the initial estimates. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, FRED series PAYEMS.

The Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index (not seasonally adjusted) rose about 129.6% from January 2012 to June 2022, from 134.157 to 308.055 (index, January 2000 = 100). Source: S&P Dow Jones Indices (S&P Cotality Case-Shiller), FRED series CSUSHPINSA.

The most negative daily 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread in 2023 was -1.08 percentage points, on July 3, 2023. The next deepest was -1.07 on March 8, 2023. Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, calculated from Treasury constant maturity yields, FRED series T10Y2Y.

3 quarters from 2020 through 2024 had negative annualized real GDP growth on currently published data: Q1 2020 (-5.2%), Q2 2020 (-28.0%) and Q1 2022 (-1.0%), all seasonally adjusted annual rates. Q2 2022 was originally reported as negative but has since been revised to +0.6%, so older sources may count 4. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA.

Initial jobless claims peaked in 2020 at 6,137,000 (seasonally adjusted) for the week ending Saturday, April 4, 2020. This is the currently published, revised figure. Source: U.S. Employment and Training Administration (Department of Labor), FRED series ICSA.
